overview: Qualitative interpretive description study of induction scheduling on one labour and birth unit, with interviews and focus groups across the booking chain and interviews with women who had a delayed induction.
population: Staff: midwives, obstetricians, labour ward coordinators, booking clerks and bed managers. Women: aged 18 or over, 6 weeks to 12 months after a birth in which induction started more than 12 hours after the booked time.
exposure: Experience of the current booking and start process for induction of labour.
procedures: Semi-structured interviews of 45 to 60 minutes and two staff focus groups of 6 to 8 people in protected study time; interviews with women at home, by telephone or by video, with interpreters; a distress protocol with pause, stop and referral to the birth reflections service.

outcomes.name: Account of how scheduling shapes delay, workload and experience
outcomes.measure: Themes from reflexive thematic analysis, mapped to booking steps in a framework matrix
outcomes.why: Answers the study question and feeds redesign.

outcomes.name: Redesign recommendations
outcomes.measure: Recommendations rated for feasibility by the unit's redesign group
outcomes.why: The unit manager asked for practical output.

outcomes.name: Sample coverage
outcomes.measure: Participants by role, shift pattern, parity, ethnicity and language
outcomes.why: Shows whether hard-to-reach voices were heard.

outcomes.name: Participant distress
outcomes.measure: Interviews paused or stopped and referrals to support
outcomes.why: Interviews about difficult births can cause harm.

feasibility: About 20 staff interviews, 2 focus groups and 12 to 15 interviews with women within one protected day per week over nine months.
biasMitigation: Interviewer does not manage the participants
Reflexive journal kept by the lead midwife
Recruitment of women through community midwives as well as the unit

biasFlags.label: Insider researcher
biasFlags.note: The lead midwife works on the unit; a co-analyst from outside the unit checks coding.

biasFlags.label: Recruitment bias among women
biasFlags.note: Women with the worst experiences may decline; purposive recruitment through community routes.

flags: Covariates are not applicable to a qualitative design
parsimony.simplestPath: One study question, interviews across the booking chain, one framework matrix.

theoreticalFramework: Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety (SEIPS) to organise themes by work system component: people, tasks, tools, organisation and environment.
summary: Interpretive description with one primary account, one secondary output, sample coverage and a distress safeguard.
